issues.suggestion: TurboQuant was already covered two days ago. The new angle here is the stock market impact (~$100bi wiped from memory stocks). issues.current_text: AstraZeneca tozorakimab (primeiro biológico anti-IL-33), FDA aprovou Kresladi, Artemis II launch
issues.previous_text: FDA aprovou Lifyorli, Kodiak Zenkuda alcançou melhoria, Viking VK2735 completou recrutamento (03-27); FDA aprovou AVLAYAH (03-26); Olatec dapansutrila fase 2 (03-25)
issues.suggestion: Every edition closes with a pharma/science grab-bag paragraph. The structure is identical: 2-3 trial results or approvals stacked end-to-end. Readers will start skimming this section. Try: integrate the most impactful pharma story into the main narrative (tozorakimab as first anti-IL-33 biologic for COPD is genuinely significant), or open a different section with science/space news instead of always closing with it.

issues.previous_text: primeiro robotáxi comercial da Europa (03-27) / primeiro sistema de pesquisa autônoma a passar por revisão por pares (03-26) / primeiro tratamento para a síndrome de Hunter em 20 anos (03-26) / primeiro voo orbital privado europeu (03-25) / primeiro processador para venda direta (03-25)
issues.suggestion: The 'primeiro/first-ever' superlative appears 3 times in today's draft and 5+ times across the prior three editions. It's becoming a tic. Reserve 'primeiro' for genuinely historic firsts (Artemis II qualifies). For the others, describe the significance without the 'primeiro' crutch — e.g., 'tozorakimab é o único biológico anti-IL-33 com eficácia em DPOC' reads stronger than flagging it as a first.

issues.current_text: A OpenAI respondeu com plugins para o Codex integrando Slack, Figma e Notion ao assistente de 1,6 milhão de usuários semanais
issues.previous_text: Competitive response framing recurs: Google imports ChatGPT/Claude data (03-27), Apple opens Siri to rivals (03-27), OpenAI Foundation $1B vs Anthropic (03-26)
issues.suggestion: The 'Company X respondeu/reagiu' competitive framing makes every product launch sound reactive. Present OpenAI's Codex plugins on their own merits — what they do and why they matter — without framing them as a response to Claude Mythos. The reader can connect the dots.

summary: Two fully repeated stories (TurboQuant, Agile-DeepMind partnership), two partially repeated stories (Iran ceasefire rejection, Meta 700 layoffs), and structural patterns (data center megadeal lists, pharma closing paragraph, 'primeiro' overuse, competitive-response framing) that make editions sound interchangeable.
